hypothesis: Randomized contact friction, body mass and small velocity kicks improve robustness to held-out dynamics without changing the reward or PPO algorithm.
checkpoint_selection: final fixed-budget checkpoint, no selection on evaluation results
notes: These are self-designed held-out stress tests, not the undisclosed TA evaluation environment.
Friction and mass are sampled per collision shape/body at startup; fixed within each parallel training environment.
Ground friction=1 and multiply combination are shared across methods; nominal material is explicitly standardized.
A kick adds uniform x/y velocity offsets; it is not a measured force in newtons.
Population SD over 100 episodes differs from variability across independently trained seeds.
